# wb reference

<!-- Generated by docs/gen-wb.mjs from `wb tools --json`; do not edit by hand. -->

`wb` is the agent command inside a sandbox (`/opt/workbox/bin/wb`, on `PATH`). It talks only to
the in-box runner on `/run/workbox/runner.sock`; brokered subcommands are relayed to the host.
Every subcommand accepts `--help` and `--json`. With `--json`, a command prints one JSON value
on stdout, and a failure prints `{"error": {"code", "message", "data"?}}` there instead.
Diagnostics go to stderr. `wb help <command>` and `wb <command> --help` print the usage below.

## Commands

| Command      | Summary                                                            | Usage                                                                             |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`     | Sandbox id, boot id, limits, usage and network mode                | `wb status [--json]`                                                              |
| `tools`      | List every wb subcommand                                           | `wb tools [--json]`                                                               |
| `help`       | Show help for wb or one subcommand                                 | `wb help [command]`                                                               |
| `session`    | Durable sessions: start\|list\|attach\|input\|stop                 | `wb session start [--name n] [--cwd d] [--env K=V] [--pty] -- <cmd...>`           |
| `run`        | Run a command and record an evidence envelope                      | `wb run -- <cmd...>`                                                              |
| `ask`        | Ask a human: raise\|status\|list\|wait                             | `wb ask raise --kind question\|decision\|permission\|secret [--option o] <title>` |
| `secret`     | Brokered secrets: exec\|list (values injected into the child only) | `wb secret exec <ref>... -- <cmd...> \| wb secret list`                           |
| `event`      | Append a structured event                                          | `wb event emit <type> [json]`                                                     |
| `lease`      | Lease status\|renew                                                | `wb lease status \| wb lease renew [--ttl-ms n]`                                  |
| `checkpoint` | Checkpoint create\|list                                            | `wb checkpoint create [--name n] \| wb checkpoint list`                           |
| `artifact`   | Artifacts: put\|get\|list                                          | `wb artifact put <file> \| get <sha256> [dest] \| list`                           |
| `net`        | Network policy\|test                                               | `wb net policy \| wb net test <host> <port>`                                      |
| `preset`     | Toolchain presets: list\|install                                   | `wb preset list \| wb preset install <web\|python\|rust\|go\|system\|agents>`     |

## Exit codes

A failed wb call exits with the status its protocol error code maps to (`exitCodeFor` in
packages/wb/src/main.js):

| Exit | Meaning                                                                        | Error codes                                                                                                            |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | success                                                                        |                                                                                                                        |
| 1    | internal error, and every code not mapped to another status                    | `E_LINE_TOO_LONG`, `E_CANCELLED`, `E_INTERNAL`, `E_CONFLICT`, `E_GAP`, `E_UNSUPPORTED`, `E_BUSY`, `E_LIMIT`, `E_STATE` |
| 2    | usage: bad arguments, unknown command or method, unparsable input              | `E_PARSE`, `E_UNKNOWN_METHOD`, `E_INVALID_PARAMS`                                                                      |
| 3    | not found                                                                      | `E_NOT_FOUND`                                                                                                          |
| 4    | denied or unavailable: policy refusal, quarantined sandbox, no control channel | `E_CLOSED`, `E_DENIED`, `E_QUARANTINED`, `E_UNAVAILABLE`                                                               |
| 5    | timeout                                                                        | `E_TIMEOUT`                                                                                                            |

`wb run`, `wb secret exec` and `wb session attach` on a finished session exit with the
wrapped command's own status instead: its exit code, or 128 + the signal number when it died
by a signal (SIGTERM gives 143, SIGKILL gives 137).
